text:
anna: Quick Q — for the upcoming quant bakeoff (FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ) should we treat the calibration set as a single pooled corpus or as a stratified mixture with heavy edgecase weighting?

mike: my vote is stratified. we saw INT8 regressions concentrated in long-code prompts and low-resource languages last time.

sarah: +1 stratified. also recommend explicit negative controls (nonsense prompts / model-breaking inputs) to catch hallucination amplification after quant.

ryan: can we be concrete about strata? i propose: 1) short convo, 2) long code, 3) multi-turn instruction, 4) math/structured, 5) low-resource L1, 6) adversarial phrasing. allocate 40/20/15/10/10/5 pct respectively.

anna: that split looks reasonable. question: do we keep the same seeds across quant variants for comparability or temper seeds per-profile (seed-tempering) to stress distribution sensitivity?

jen: keep seeds fixed for base comparability, but add a small tempered resample per-stratum (e.g., 3 extra seeded draws) so we can estimate variance across sampling. label them in eval metadata.

mike: agreed. metadata should include: sample_seed, stratum, original_dataset_id, prompt-template-id, and a boolean `negative_control`. makes analysis queries easy.

sarah: for negative controls i suggest two classes: syntactic garbage (`lorem-xyz`) and semantic traps (contradictory context). small set (50-100) but repeated across all runs.

rita-bot: deploy-note: added `calib_pool_v3` with strata tags and negative_control flag to S3: s3://redwood-evals/calib/calib_pool_v3.csv

ryan: nice. next — prompt curation rules: 1) anonymize PII, 2) keep prompt length distribution matching production tails, 3) include templated variants (few-shot, zero-shot, instruction).

anna: on templated variants: do we expand each original prompt into a few-shot and an instruction-flip? that multiplies eval size a lot.

jen: instead of full expansion, do a 1:4 sampling where 25% of examples get templated variants. ensures coverage without explosion.

mike: don't forget to add explicit deployment-profile labels: `hosted-low-latency`, `dedicated-burst`, `private-high-accuracy`. these map to kernel/quant-family combos in the bakeoff.

sarah: evaluation metrics: token-levenshtein for code, BLEU/EM where applicable, harmlessness classification, scalar hallucination score (human+model). compute delta relative to fp16 baseline and track signed CI.

anna: can someone paste the sample command we should use to generate the stratified holdouts?

mike: sure:```bash
python tools/sample_calib.py \
  --pool s3://redwood-evals/calib/calib_pool_v3.csv \
  --strata "short_convo:0.4,long_code:0.2,multi_turn:0.15,math:0.1,low_resource:0.1,adv:0.05" \
  --seed 42 \
  --tempered-resamples 3 \
  --negative-controls 100 \
  --out samples/calib_holdouts_v1.jsonl
```

ryan: perfect. add a column `holdout_id` and make sure holdout id is stable across runs.

sarah: final ask — for the reporting notebook include per-stratum confusion matrices and waterfall plots for accuracy delta by token position. those highlight where quantization hurts long-context generation.

anna: ok i'll assemble a short playbook: sampling command, schema, example notebook links, and a checklist for pre-bakeoff sanity checks. aiming to run first bakeoff on Monday.

jen: ping me once playbook is up, i'll schedule the human evals for hallucination checks. :white_check_mark:

mike: thanks all. tiny follow-up: can ops add an autoscaling test for `dedicated-burst` profile so perf noise is stable?

sampling-bot: noted. created ticket INF-3124 for autoscale test.

anna: awesome — i'll post the playbook link here when ready.

ryan: thanks! :rocket:
